title: Azure DNS: public and private zones
learningObjective: Host public DNS zones in Azure DNS, delegate domains, manage record sets including alias records, and configure private DNS zones with virtual network links and autoregistration.
foundation: DNS turns names (www.contoso.com) into IP addresses. Azure DNS hosts your DNS zones on Microsoft's global name servers.
Public zones answer internet queries. Private DNS zones answer only for VNets you link to them.
engineer: Delegation: buying a domain stays with your registrar; after creating the zone in Azure, update the domain's NS records at the registrar to the four Azure name servers shown on the zone (ns1-0x.azure-dns.com/.net/.org/.info). Child zones are delegated with NS records in the parent zone.

Record sets: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, SOA, SRV, TXT, CAA. A CNAME can't be at the zone apex (@) and can't share a name with other records. Alias records (A/AAAA/CNAME) point to Azure resources (public IP, Traffic Manager, Front Door, another record set) and can be used at the apex; they update automatically when the resource's IP changes.
TTL (seconds) controls how long resolvers cache answers; lower it before planned changes. Azure DNS doesn't sell domain names: buy them from a registrar (or App Service domains).

Private DNS zones: link to VNets with virtual network links. Autoregistration on a link creates A records for VMs in that VNet; a VNet can have autoregistration with only one private zone but can be linked (resolution) to many. Resolution needs Azure-provided DNS (168.63.129.16) or custom DNS servers that forward to it.
Azure DNS Private Resolver provides inbound/outbound endpoints for hybrid name resolution without DNS VMs.

example.title: Moving contoso.com to Azure DNS
body: The team creates the zone, recreates all records, lowers TTLs, then switches NS records at the registrar. The apex points to the web load balancer's public IP with an alias A record, so it follows IP changes automatically.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription and a resource group (rg-net)
permissions: DNS Zone Contributor for public zones; Private DNS Zone Contributor for private zones (plus Network Contributor on the VNet to link)
limits: Autoregistration: one private zone per VNet
Record sets per zone: see Azure DNS limits
portal: Create a resource > DNS zone: contoso.com. Note the four name servers.
Zone > + Record set: name, type, TTL, values (or alias to an Azure resource).
Private DNS zones > Create contoso.internal > Virtual network links > Add, enable auto registration.
configuration.cli:
az network dns zone create -g rg-net -n contoso.com
az network dns zone show -g rg-net -n contoso.com --query nameServers
az network dns record-set a add-record -g rg-net -z contoso.com -n www -a 20.10.1.5 --ttl 3600
az network dns record-set a create -g rg-net -z contoso.com -n @ --target-resource $(az network public-ip show -g rg-net -n pip-web --query id -o tsv)
az network private-dns zone create -g rg-net -n contoso.internal
az network private-dns link vnet create -g rg-net -z contoso.internal -n link-app -v vnet-app -e true
configuration.powershell:
New-AzDnsZone -Name contoso.com -ResourceGroupName rg-net
New-AzDnsRecordSet -Name www -RecordType A -ZoneName contoso.com -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Ttl 3600 -DnsRecords (New-AzDnsRecordConfig -IPv4Address 20.10.1.5)
New-AzPrivateDnsZone -Name contoso.internal -ResourceGroupName rg-net
New-AzPrivateDnsVirtualNetworkLink -ZoneName contoso.internal -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name link-app -VirtualNetworkId (Get-AzVirtualNetwork -Name vnet-app -ResourceGroupName rg-net).Id -EnableRegistration

lab.objective: Delegate a public zone, add apex and www records, and resolve VM names privately.
steps: Public DNS zone: run the default (CNAME at apex, not delegated).
Private DNS zone: apply 'Link with autoregistration', then 'Custom DNS without forwarding'.
expected: No CNAME at the apex: use alias
Private zones need links and Azure DNS

validation.text: Created an alias record at the apex

lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Records exist in Azure but the internet sees old values.
troubleshooting.cause: Domain not delegated, or old TTL still cached.
troubleshooting.fix: Update NS at the registrar; wait for TTL.

troubleshooting.symptom: VMs can't resolve private zone names.
troubleshooting.cause: No virtual network link, or custom DNS not forwarding to 168.63.129.16.

comparisons.difference: AWS DNS with public and private hosted zones; alias records are similar.
Resolves VM names within one VNet only; private zones span VNets with custom names.

misconceptions.myth: Azure DNS makes you the domain's registrar.
misconceptions.reality: You still buy the domain from a registrar (or App Service Domains).

misconceptions.myth: Autoregistration can be enabled in many zones for one VNet.
misconceptions.reality: Only one autoregistration zone per VNet.

architectureDecisions: Use alias records for apex records pointing to Azure resources.
Centralise private DNS zones and link spokes.
Use DNS Private Resolver for hybrid resolution.

Private DNS zones and VNet links

steps.label: Names
steps.title: People and apps use names, not IPs
body: Customers type contoso.com. VMs should find db01 by name, and the names must update when IPs change.

steps.label: Public zone
steps.title: Public DNS zones
body: A public zone holds the records for a domain: A and AAAA (addresses), CNAME (alias name), MX (mail), TXT (verification), plus NS and SOA created automatically. Azure DNS hosts the zone; it does not sell domains.

steps.label: Delegate
steps.title: Delegate the domain to Azure
body: At your registrar, replace the domain's name servers with the four Azure name servers shown on the zone. For a subdomain, add NS records in the parent zone.

steps.label: Private zone
steps.title: Private DNS zones for VNets
body: A private zone resolves names only inside VNets that are linked to it. Turn on auto-registration on a link and VMs' names are added and updated automatically (one auto-registration zone per VNet).

steps.label: Alias
steps.title: Alias records follow Azure resources
body: An alias record points at an Azure resource (public IP, Traffic Manager, Front Door) instead of a fixed address, and updates when the resource changes. It can also be used at the zone apex, where CNAMEs are not allowed.

callout.text: Azure-provided DNS (168.63.129.16) is what VMs use by default.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Azure DNS
body: Public zones for the internet; private zones for VNets.
recap: Records: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA
Delegate by changing NS at the registrar
Private zones work only in linked VNets
Alias records track Azure resources, even at the apex

handsOn.title: Create public and private DNS zones and query them
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. Each DNS zone costs about US$0.50 per month.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A virtual network vnet-lab (10.10.0.0/16) in rg-az104-lab with a subnet snet-app (10.10.1.0/24): Virtual networks > + Create > IP addresses tab. For these labs, untick 'Enable private subnet' on snet-app so lab VMs can reach the internet (in production use a NAT gateway instead).

A small Linux VM vm-lab in snet-app of vnet-lab: Virtual machines > + Create. Image Ubuntu 24.04, size Standard_B1s, password authentication, Networking tab: vnet-lab / snet-app, public IP: None, NIC network security group: Basic, public inbound ports: None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead.

steps.do: Search 'DNS zones' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name lab<yourinitials>.com (any name; you do not need to own it). Create.
steps.see: The zone with four name servers like ns1-01.azure-dns.com.

steps.do: Open the zone > + Record set. Name www, type A, IP 203.0.113.10, TTL 1 hour. Add.
Cloud Shell: nslookup www.lab<yourinitials>.com <first name server from the zone>
steps.see: The answer 203.0.113.10, straight from Azure DNS.

steps.do: Search 'Private DNS zones' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name contoso.internal. Create.
Open contoso.internal > DNS Management > Virtual network links > + Add. Name link-lab, VNet vnet-lab, tick 'Enable auto registration'. Create.
Open contoso.internal > Recordsets after a minute.
steps.see: An A record for vm-lab with its private IP, added automatically.

steps.do: Run a command without SSH: open the VM > Operations > Run command > RunShellScript, type the command, Run. Run: nslookup vm-lab.contoso.internal
steps.see: The VM's private IP, resolved by Azure-provided DNS.

check: The public zone answers for www; the private zone auto-registered the VM.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
